item.title: COLLEGE BASKETBALL: Misericordia men drop MAC game at Arcadia
item.description: The Misericordia men’s basketball team had a chance to pick up ground on Arcadia in the MAC Freedom standings. The Knights had other plans. Arcadia jumped out to a 35-19 lead after one half, and picked up a 74-60 win over the Cougars on Wednesday night at Alumni Gymnasium. Arcadia is now 7-2 in the league, while Miseri falls to 6-3. item.title: HS ROUNDUP: Boylan, Chimock lead Royals past Trojanettes
item.description: The Holy Redeemer girls basketball team picked up a win over first-place Nanticoke Area on Wednesday night. Bella Boylan and McKenzie Chimock combined for 42 points as the Royals got past Nanticoke Area, 59-52, in Wyoming Vallley Conference Division 2 play. Nanticoke already wrapped up first place in the division, but Redeemer is fighting for the division’s second spot in the playoffs. item.title: GIRLS BASKETBALL: Fourth-quarter free throws help Crestwood seal win over Dallas
item.description: WRIGHT TWP. — Mary Mushock Namey is a firm believer that it doesn’t matter how you start the season, but rather how you finish it. The same could be said for the Comets on Wednesday night. It wasn’t how they wanted to shoot from the free throw line in the beginning of the game, it was a case of making them when they counted at the end. item.title: AHL: Penguins score four in the third to top Hershey
item.description: It took until the third period before the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins got the offense going. But once it got rolling, the Hershey Bears couldn’t stop it. The Pens scored three unanswered goals in the the final 13 minutes Wednesday night to top Hershey, 4-1, at Mohegan Arena at Casey Plaza. Wilkes-Barre/Scranton has now won five straight over the Bears to improve to 6-1 against their rivals this season.
